clue.text: A mineral — the thing put in a dish

indicators.note: put in tells us the thing goes inside the dish phrase

parts.note: a pâté is a dish of meat or fish paste, so 'a dish' gives A PATE
it is the pronoun for a thing

explanation.surface: A rock specimen served up as if it were food on a plate.
explanation.walkthrough: The opening A belongs to the definition, while the A in 'a dish' joins PATE; IT sits inside to make A PAT-IT-E.
explanation.definitionFit: Apatite is a phosphate mineral found in rocks, bones and teeth.

clue.text: Official gets to stride around making introduction

indicators.note: around means the stride word goes round the official

parts.note: to pace is to stride
a ref is a referee, a match official

explanation.surface: A referee pacing about before opening proceedings.
explanation.definitionFit: A preface is the opening section of a book, introducing what follows.

clue.text: Law of Moses coming from a rocky height — gosh!

parts.note: a tor is a rocky hill, as on Dartmoor
ah is an exclamation of surprise

explanation.surface: Moses brings the law down from a rocky mountain to astonishment.
explanation.definitionFit: The Torah is the Jewish law, the five books traditionally attributed to Moses.

clue.text: Provider of booze creating spill around street

indicators.note: around means the spill goes round the street

parts.note: a spill is a thin strip for lighting, like a taper

explanation.surface: A barman causing a spillage out in the road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spill' suggests slopping drink, but it is the thin lighting strip.
explanation.definitionFit: A tapster draws beer from the barrel, a bartender who serves drinks.

clue.text: Sink as container for domestic fuel

definitions.meaning: to sink a ship deliberately by holing it
a bucket for carrying coal to the household fire

explanation.surface: A sink apparently doubling as a coal bucket in the kitchen.
explanation.definitionFit: Scuttling a vessel sinks it on purpose; a coal bucket by the hearth bears the same name.

clue.text: Programmers scored after rescheduling

indicators.note: rescheduling means the letters of scored are put in a new order

explanation.surface: Software developers got a result once the match was rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Coders write computer code, which is what programmers do.

clue.text: Sailor the woman caught in wickedness upsettingly taints

parts.note: a tar is a sailor

indicators.note: caught in means the woman is held inside the wickedness
upsettingly in a down clue means turned upside down, reversed

parts.note: sin is wickedness
she is the woman

explanation.surface: A sailor and a woman embroiled in vice, which sullies reputations.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'upsettingly' means read upwards, giving NIS; 'taints' reads as a noun in the surface but is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To tarnish is to dull or spoil, just as to taint is to sully.

clue.text: The French fellow at match gets space to manoeuvre

parts.note: le is French for the
the groom is the man at a wedding, a match

explanation.surface: A Frenchman at a football match finds room to move.
explanation.walkthrough: 'match' is a marriage, not a game.
explanation.definitionFit: Legroom is room to stretch one's legs, space to move about.

clue.text: Mates lounging around as members of an old sect

indicators.note: around suggests the letters of the mates lounging are scattered about

explanation.surface: Friends idling about, as followers of some religion.
explanation.definitionFit: Muggletonians were a small Puritan sect founded in 17th-century London by Lodowicke Muggleton.

clue.text: Ill-mannered type with short hair

indicators.note: short means the hair word is cut off before its final letter

parts.note: a beard is hair on the chin

explanation.surface: A rude person with a cropped haircut.
explanation.definitionFit: A boorish, grumpy person is called a bear, as in 'like a bear with a sore head'.

clue.text: Heartless chum, too young for stealing

indicators.note: heartless means the middle letter of the friend word is removed

parts.note: a chum is a pal
too young to be legally allowed something is underage

explanation.surface: A callous friend, still a minor, caught thieving.
explanation.definitionFit: Plunderage is an old word for pillage or embezzlement of goods, especially at sea: theft.

clue.text: Prestige of store by road junction

parts.note: a cache is a hidden store
a T-junction is where one road meets another

explanation.surface: A shop gains status from its location at a crossroads.
explanation.definitionFit: Cachet is distinction or social standing, the kind of status that makes something desirable.

clue.text: No gentleman, guy retreating in fortified place

indicators.note: retreating means going backwards, so the assembled letters are read in reverse

parts.note: sir is the title of a gentleman or knight
to guy someone is to mock or rag them

explanation.surface: A man who is no gentleman backs away into a stronghold.
explanation.definitionFit: A garrison is a town or fort manned by troops, so a defended post.

clue.text: New gate leading to forest that offers outdoor refreshments

indicators.note: leading to puts the first part in front of the second
new suggests the letters of gate are made into a fresh arrangement

parts.note: Arden is the forest in Shakespeare's As You Like It, in Warwickshire

explanation.surface: A fresh gate opening on to woodland where a café serves visitors outside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New' rearranges GATE into TEA, which leads into ARDEN.
explanation.definitionFit: A tea garden is an open-air café garden where drinks and cakes are served.

clue.text: Seek pleasure, having good time ensnaring completely terrible ruler

indicators.note: ensnaring means the outer letters trap the ruler phrase

parts.note: all means completely
Ivan the Terrible was a tsar of Russia

explanation.surface: A pleasure-seeker enjoys themselves while trapping a tyrant.
explanation.definitionFit: To gallivant is to roam around enjoying oneself, chasing amusement.

clue.text: A false statement about dwarf Tom's digital protection

parts.words: A false statement about dwarf Tom's
parts.note: saying the tiny Tom ... of folklore is tall would be untrue, and that phrase spells the answer

explanation.surface: A lie told about a famous tiny man, somehow linked to finger-guarding.
explanation.walkthrough: Tom Thumb is the thumb-sized hero of an English folk tale, so calling him tall is a false statement.
explanation.definitionFit: A thumbstall is a sheath worn over an injured thumb, protecting a digit.

clue.text: See 16
Nervous model losing heart to enchantress

indicators.note: the inner part of the model's name gives way to the enchantress

parts.note: Twiggy is the famous 1960s British fashion model
an enchantress is a witch

explanation.surface: An anxious fashion model loses her nerve to a sorceress.
explanation.walkthrough: All but the outer T and Y of TWIGGY are replaced.
explanation.definitionFit: Twitchy describes someone jumpy and on edge, the state of being anxious.

clue.text: Male's attempt to get behind partner's specious reasoning

indicators.note: getting behind means coming after the partner part

parts.note: SOP is short for significant other person, a partner
his is the male possessive
a try is an attempt

explanation.surface: A man trying to hide behind his partner's flawed argument.
explanation.definitionFit: Sophistry is clever but deceptive argument, reasoning that sounds plausible yet is unsound.

clue.text: Not much of a drink, doubly hard to swallow it

indicators.note: to swallow places the drink phrase within the pair of letters
doubly means the hard letter appears twice

parts.note: H stands for hard, as on pencils
port is a fortified wine

explanation.surface: A tiny drink that's hard to get down.
explanation.definitionFit: A ha'porth is a halfpennyworth, an old British expression for a very small amount.

clue.text: Gatherings of king and supporters

parts.note: R stands for Rex, king
allies support each other

explanation.surface: A monarch and his followers holding meetings.
explanation.definitionFit: Rallies are mass meetings of people assembled for a cause.

clue.text: Hadrian type, wanting length set up in state of conflict?

indicators.note: in puts the raised length inside the conflict word

parts.note: war is a state of armed conflict

indicators.note: set up in a down clue means written upwards, reversed

parts.note: an ell is an old measure of cloth length

explanation.surface: A Roman emperor lacking a measure of length during wartime.
explanation.walkthrough: Emperor Hadrian built a wall across northern England; 'wanting' is just a link here.
explanation.definitionFit: A waller is a builder of walls, as Hadrian famously was.

clue.text: No one needing meat around before one gets rice dish

indicators.note: before places the reversed part ahead of the final one
around means the run of letters is turned the other way

parts.note: nay means no
I is the Roman numeral one
a rib is a cut of meat
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A vegetarian, refusing meat, gets a rice meal instead.
explanation.definitionFit: Biriyani is a South Asian dish of spiced rice cooked with meat or vegetables.

clue.text: Sounds like cushion will get a bit wet

indicators.note: sounds like says the spoken form is what counts

parts.note: a pad is a cushion; will contracts to 'll

explanation.surface: A cushion left out will get damp.
explanation.definitionFit: To paddle is to wade in shallow water, getting only the feet and ankles wet.

clue.text: Beginning university beset by unfortunate financial situation

indicators.note: beset by means surrounded by, so the university goes inside

parts.note: debt is owing money

explanation.surface: A student starting university already in debt.
explanation.definitionFit: A debut is a first appearance or launch, the start of a career.

clue.text: It has cabins; it's possibly nicer alone

indicators.note: possibly hints that the letters of nicer alone can take another form

explanation.surface: Something with cabins might be pleasanter on its own.
explanation.definitionFit: A passenger ship carrying travellers has cabins where they sleep.

clue.text: One of four involved in a game offering security

definitions.text: One of four involved in a game
definitions.meaning: cricket has two wickets, each topped by two small crosspieces, four in all
money pledged so an accused is released before trial

explanation.surface: A sporting item somehow guaranteeing safety.
explanation.walkthrough: Cricket's two wickets each carry two bails, small wooden pieces resting on the stumps.
explanation.definitionFit: Bail is money deposited as a guarantee that a defendant will return to court.

clue.text: Loveless person giving away nothing in this writer's thriller

indicators.note: in places the trimmed person inside the possessive

parts.note: the setter's own, so my

indicators.note: love is zero in tennis, the letter O, which is removed

parts.note: an oyster is a tight-lipped, secretive person

explanation.surface: A lonely, secretive character appears in the author's suspense novel.
explanation.definitionFit: A mystery is a detective or suspense story, a genre close to the thriller.

clue.text: Most virtuous dealer, maybe, embracing success

indicators.note: embracing means holding the success word inside

parts.note: in bridge, West is one of the four players, any of whom might deal
a hit is a success

explanation.surface: The most honest card dealer has a winning streak.
explanation.definitionFit: Whitest suggests purest and most blameless, as in whiter than white.
